subject.title: [Bug]: Agent self-update bypasses update.run and uses raw npm global upgrade without restarting gateway

question: Should the raw global OpenClaw package-manager self-update guard be accepted as a hard exec-side block in the shared exec-control guard, or should maintainers choose a softer restart-guarantee path?
rationale: The issue is maintainer-authored/protected, the remaining fix is already paired with an open PR, and the enforcement choice can intentionally break existing exec-based operator update workflows.

options.title: Rework and land shared guard
options.body: Move the candidate detector into the shared exec-control guard, cover exec and exec-review consumers, require real behavior proof, and close this issue after merge.

options.title: Choose softer restart enforcement
options.body: Keep raw package-manager updates possible only if the implementation can prove a safe gateway restart before reporting success.

options.title: Keep paused behind maintainer policy
options.body: Leave this issue open while maintainers decide the permanent self-update enforcement boundary and do not queue another repair PR.

recommendation.title: Rework and land shared guard
recommendation.body: Move the candidate detector into the shared exec-control guard, cover exec and exec-review consumers, require real behavior proof, and close this issue after merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the maintainer-associated report, supplied the incident evidence, and framed the accepted fix directions.
